label: inferior vena cava leiomyosarcoma
definition: An aggressive malignant smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the inferior vena cava, characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic spindle cells.

label: pediatric Crohn disease
definition: A Crohn disease with onset before adulthood, characterized by a greater frequency of extensive ileocolonic and upper gastrointestinal involvement than adult-onset disease, and by growth failure and pubertal delay; management must address linear growth, nutrition and pubertal development in addition to induction and maintenance of remission.

label: Refsum disease, classic
definition: An adult Refsum disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PHYH gene.

label: low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
definition: An ovarian serous carcinoma characterized by low-grade cytologic features, infrequent mitotic figures and slow tumor growth, which is thought to develop from a serous borderline ovarian tumor. It shows an activated mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway with KRAS and BRAF mutations and only rarely TP53 mutations, and is a distinct entity from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma rather than a grade of it. It accounts for 2-5% of ovarian carcinomas and 5-10% of serous ovarian carcinomas.

label: tetrahydrobiopterin-unresponsive phenylketonuria
definition: A phenylketonuria in which blood phenylalanine concentrations do not fall substantially (conventionally defined as a reduction of more than 30%) in response to an oral tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride) loading test, so that treatment with BH4 is not effective and phenylalanine-restricted dietary management remains necessary.

label: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency
definition: A disorder of phenylalanine metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the PAH gene, encompassing the full spectrum of phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency from mild hyperphenylalaninemia, which requires no treatment, to phenylketonuria, in which untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations warrant phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment.

label: juvenile ossifying fibroma
definition: An ossifying fibroma arising predominantly in children and young adults, comprising two histological variants: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma and psammomatoid ossifying fibroma.

label: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma
definition: A juvenile ossifying fibroma predominantly arises in children and adolescents. It is characterized by prominent osteoid formation rimmed by osteoblasts in a fibrotic stroma. Patients usually present with painless jaw expansion that is associated with rapid growth and tooth displacement.

label: psammomatoid ossifying fibroma
definition: A juvenile ossifying fibroma arises usually affects individuals in their second to fourth decades with no sex predilection. It is characterized by the presence of multiple ossicles resembling psammoma bodies in a hypercellular stroma.

label: SMARCB1-related tumor predisposition
definition: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.

label: severe chronic neutropenia
definition: A neutropenia characterized by persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x 10^9/L lasting for at least 3 months, not explained by medication use, infection or another underlying condition, and associated with recurrent and potentially life-threatening bacterial infections. The major clinical subtypes include congenital, cyclic, idiopathic, and autoimmune neutropenia, which share common diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and long-term follow-up.

label: severe idiopathic neutropenia
definition: An idiopathic form of severe chronic neutropenia that cannot be classified as congenital, cyclic or autoimmune neutropenia, and is not explained by drug exposure, bone marrow failure, malignancy or systemic autoimmune disease. Symptoms are usually less severe than in congenital neutropenia, but infections can be life-threatening in some patients.

label: severe autoimmune neutropenia
definition: An autoimmune form of severe chronic neutropenia in which neutrophil-specific antibodies increase the destruction of circulating neutrophils, in the absence of systemic autoimmune disease. It is most common in children aged 6 months to 4 years, and it can also occur in adults. Serious bacterial infections are infrequent.

label: fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome
definition: A skeletal system disorder caused by a variation in the GNAS gene, characterized by involvement of the skin, skeleton and certain endocrine organs. Fibrous dysplasia ranges from an isolated monostotic lesion to severe polyostotic disease. McCune-Albright syndrome is diagnosed when fibrous dysplasia occurs with at least one extra-skeletal feature, or when two or more extra-skeletal features occur alone. The condition is not inherited. The signs and symptoms associated with the disorder vary greatly from person to person, depending upon the specific body cells and tissues that are affected by the gene variant.

label: posterior ischemic optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder characterized by ischemic injury to the retrobulbar (posterior) portion of the optic nerve, presenting with sudden visual loss and an initially normal-appearing optic disc, in contrast to anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. It may be arteritic (due to giant cell arteritis), nonarteritic, or surgical (following a surgical procedure).

label: traumatic optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by closed or penetrating trauma to the face or head that injures the optic nerve, resulting in visual loss, often with an afferent pupillary defect.

label: radiation-induced optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by radiation necrosis of the anterior visual pathway, occurring as a late complication of radiotherapy for head and neck or intracranial tumours and resulting in acute, painless and usually irreversible visual loss. Onset is typically 10 to 20 months after treatment but ranges from 3 months to 9 years.

label: compressive optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by mechanical compression of the optic nerve or chiasm along its course, for example by orbital or intracranial tumours, sinus mucoceles or thyroid eye disease, resulting in progressive visual loss.

label: ophthalmic artery occlusion
definition: An ocular vascular disorder characterized by acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid artery, leading to severe ischemia of the globe and associated ocular tissues. It can resemble central retinal artery occlusion with additional choroidal ischemia, and may cause sudden and permanent visual loss.

label: vitreomacular traction syndrome
definition: A vitreous and retinal disorder characterized by incomplete posterior vitreous detachment with persistent focal adhesion to the macula. This exerts anteroposterior traction that distorts foveal anatomy, causing structural changes such as foveal deformation, pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid, with potential progression to a macular hole.

label: traumatic macular hole
definition: A full-thickness macular hole that results from trauma, such as closed-globe or open-globe ocular injury, laser injury, surgical trauma, lightning strike or electrical shock. It occurs more often in young men, whereas idiopathic macular hole occurs more often in women older than 65 years.

label: juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis
definition: A uveitis occurring in individuals with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and its most frequent extra-articular manifestation. The most common form is chronic anterior uveitis, which is almost always asymptomatic in the initial stages, so screening of at-risk patients is essential.

label: secondary glaucoma
definition: A glaucoma in which elevation of intraocular pressure results from an identifiable pathophysiological mechanism, such as intraocular inflammation, pigment dispersion, hemorrhage, trauma, corticosteroid use or elevated episcleral venous pressure, in contrast to primary glaucoma. Secondary glaucomas form a heterogeneous group of diseases.

label: pigmentary glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma that can develop in pigment dispersion syndrome, in which pigment released from the iris is deposited in the trabecular meshwork, reducing aqueous outflow and raising intraocular pressure, leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. It is usually diagnosed between 40 and 50 years of age and occurs more often in men.

label: uveitic glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma in which optic nerve damage results from elevated intraocular pressure secondary to intraocular inflammation via trabecular inflammation/obstruction, steroid response, or synechial angle\nclosure in the setting of uveitis. Compared with primary open-angle glaucoma, it often has a more aggressive course, with very high intraocular pressure that waxes and wanes.

label: ghost cell glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma in which degenerated red blood cells (ghost cells), formed in the vitreous cavity after hemorrhage, pass forward into the anterior chamber and obstruct the aqueous outflow channels.

label: hemolytic glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma following intraocular hemorrhage, in which the trabecular meshwork is obstructed by fragments of hemolyzed red blood cells and hemoglobin-laden macrophages.

label: aniridia-associated glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma occurring in individuals with aniridia. Most affected eyes have open anterior chamber angles, and a minority have partial or complete angle closure.

label: plateau iris syndrome
definition: A form of primary angle-closure glaucoma caused by a large or anteriorly positioned ciliary body that leads to mechanical obstruction of the trabecular meshwork. It is most often found in young patients.

label: exfoliation glaucoma
definition: A secondary open-angle glaucoma that develops in individuals with exfoliation syndrome. Exfoliation syndrome is associated with raised intraocular pressure in up to 44% of patients, making it the most commonly identifiable cause of secondary open-angle glaucoma.

label: FBN1-related geleophysic and acromelic dysplasia
definition: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FBN1 gene. This condition is characterized by short stature, delayed bone age, stiff joints, acromegaly, hip dysplasia, respiratory issues (including sleep apnea and asthma), short hands/feet, and facial anomalies (such as a long philtrum, bulbous nose, broad/depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, and elongation of the eyelashes).

label: CAMK2A-related neurodevelopmental disorder
definition: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CAMK2A gene.

label: NUS1-related disorder
definition: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NUS1 gene. Biallelic variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Heterozygous variants, including deletions, cause a complex neurological disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and movement disorders including myoclonus, dystonia, ataxia, tremor and parkinsonism. Rare NUS1 variants have also been associated with Parkinson's disease.

label: human ABL1 deficiency syndrome
definition: A multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome caused by homozygous loss-of-function variants in the ABL1 gene. It is characterized by multiple congenital malformations (wormian skull bones and brachydactyly) and distinctive facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, prominent eyes, short, broad and flat nose, and macrostomia). It is allelic to, but clinically distinct from, congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome, which is caused by germline gain-of-function variants in ABL1.

label: TUBB-related tubulinopathy
definition: Any tubulinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB gene. Heterozygous TUBB variants cause two overlapping developmental disorders, complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) and congenital symmetric circumferential skin creases (CSCSC), also known as circumferential skin creases Kunze type. The clinical findings are diverse and include abnormalities of the cortex, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brain stem and cerebellum, microcephaly, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, excess skin folding and growth retardation.

label: Gianotti-Crosti syndrome
definition: An acrodermatitis characterized by the acute onset of a self-limited, symmetrical, monomorphic papular or papulovesicular eruption predominantly on the cheeks, buttocks and extensor surfaces of the extremities, with relative sparing of the trunk. It mainly affects children between 1 and 6 years of age and is considered an immunologic reaction triggered by viral infections, most commonly Epstein-Barr virus and hepatitis B virus, or occasionally by vaccination. Lesions typically resolve spontaneously within weeks without scarring.

label: polymorphous adenocarcinoma
definition: A salivary gland adenocarcinoma that arises predominantly from the minor salivary glands, most often in the palate, and rarely from the major salivary glands. It is characterized by cytologic uniformity and architectural diversity, with tumor cells showing pale to clear nuclei with inconspicuous nucleoli arranged in a wide variety of growth patterns. It commonly harbors a PRKD1 E710D mutation, typically presents as a painless, slow-growing mass, and generally has an excellent prognosis.

label: classical-like Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
definition: An Ehlers-Danlos syndrome characterized by skin hyperextensibility with velvety skin texture and absence of atrophic scarring, generalized joint hypermobility with or without recurrent dislocations, and easily bruised skin or spontaneous.

label: kyphoscoliotic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
definition: A rare systemic disease for which two subtypes exist, either related to the gene PLOD1 or FKBP14, and for which the clinically overlapping characteristics include congenital muscle hypotonia, congenital or early-onset kyphoscoliosis (progressive or non-progressive), and generalized joint hypermobility with dislocations/subluxations (in particular of the shoulders, hips, and knees). Additional features which may occur in both subtypes are skin hyperextensibility, easy bruising of the skin, rupture/aneurysm of a medium-sized artery, osteopenia/osteoporosis, blue sclerae, umbilical or inguinal hernia, chest deformity, marfanoid habitus, talipes equinovarus, and refractive errors. Gene-specific features, with variable presentation, are additionally observed in each subtype.

label: Athabaskan brainstem dysgenesis syndrome
definition: A HOXA1-related syndrome characterized by horizontal gaze palsy, sensorineural deafness, central hypoventilation, developmental delay, and intellectual disability, described in persons of Athabaskan American Indian heritage. Swallowing dysfunction, vocal cord paralysis, facial paresis, seizures, internal carotid artery, and cardiac outflow tract anomalies may be additionally observed. No dysmorphic facial features are associated.
